summary: The study describes the growth of ZnSe/ZnS strained quantum well structures on (100)-oriented Si substrates using low-pressure metalorganic atomic layer epitaxy (ALE) at 1508C. The structures exhibit high crystalline quality and optical properties, with a narrow full-width at half-maximum (FWHM) of 32 meV for the photoluminescence (PL) spectra. The process uses DMZn, H2S, and H2Se as reactants, and the results are supported by X-ray diffraction, secondary ion mass spectrometry, and photoluminescence measurements.
evidence: The ZnSe/ZnS strained single quantum well (SSQW) and strained multiple quantum well (SMQW) structures were grown on (100)-oriented Si substrates at 1508C in a horizontal cold-wall quartz reactor by low-pressure metalorganic atomic layer epitaxy (ALE) at a pressure of 30 Torr. Dimethylzinc (DMZn), hydrogen sulfide (H2S) and hydrogen selenide (H2Se) were used as the reactants. The high-quality crystalline ZnS(1000A˚)/ZnSe(7lA˚)/ZnS(1000A˚)/Si SSQW structure exhibits a 32 meV full-width at half-maximum (FWHM) for the 7K PL spectra.
